title: Leave the leaves
why: Fallen leaves shelter the insects who sparrows and other birds eat through the winter.

title: Lights out on big nights
why: Fall migration is on. Dark windows mean fewer birds crashing into glass.

title: Check pigeons' feet for string
why: String wrapped around toes cuts off circulation. The Wild Bird Fund can help if you spot one.

title: Skip the bread
why: It fills them up without feeding them. Let them forage for what their bodies need.

title: Say no to rat poison
why: Hawks and owls eat poisoned rats and die too. Sealing up gaps works without the suffering.

title: Pause before rescuing a fledgling
why: Most babies on the ground are fledglings learning to fly, with parents nearby. Watch from a distance first.

title: Keep cats inside
why: Spring is full of baby birds on the ground. Indoor cats keep them safe, and stay safe from cars themselves.

title: Pause before rescuing a fledgling
why: A feathered baby hopping on the ground is learning to fly, and their parents are nearby. Watch from a distance first.

title: Make windows visible
why: Decals, tape dots or screens on big windows stop birds from flying into the reflection of the sky.

title: Wait to trim hedges
why: Birds are nesting in bushes and trees right now. If you can, save the trimming for fall.

title: Plant something native
why: A pot of native flowers on a stoop or fire escape feeds the insects who birds feed their chicks.

title: Let the fire escape nest be
why: If birds nest on your fire escape or AC unit, give them a few weeks. The chicks will be gone soon.

title: Set out a shallow dish of water
why: On hot days, a shallow dish with a stone in it gives birds a drink and a bath. Rinse it every day.

title: Plant milkweed
why: Monarch caterpillars only eat milkweed. A single pot can raise a few butterflies.

title: Switch off the porch light
why: Every outdoor light turned off at night saves moths from circling until they're worn out.

title: Pick up fishing line
why: Lost fishing line tangles legs and wings. If you see some on the pier or beach, put it in the trash.

title: Skip lawn chemicals
why: Pesticides kill the worms and bugs who robins feed their young. A little wild grass is fine.

title: Give mom a chance
why: A baby squirrel on the ground usually has a mom coming back for them. Keep pets away and watch for a couple of hours.

title: Leave the seed heads standing
why: Dry flower stalks in planters still hold seeds. Leave them up for winter birds to pick at.

title: Use pet-safe ice melt
why: Rock salt burns paws and feet, and poisons birds who eat it. Pet-safe ice melt or sand is gentler.

title: Keep feeders clean
why: If you feed birds, wash the feeder every couple of weeks so sickness doesn't spread between them.

title: Put a lid on it
why: Tight lids keep hungry animals out of sharp cans and spoiled food during the lean months.

title: Say no to rat poison
why: Hawks and owls eat poisoned rats and die too. Sealing up gaps works without the suffering.

title: Give them room on cold days
why: Animals have little energy to spare in winter. Every time one has to flee, it costs them. Watch from a distance.
